mechanism_narrative: A sustained low level of federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which tends to boost equity markets by reducing borrowing costs and increasing risk appetite.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following a low FEDFUNDS period, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate suggests economic weakness, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns as consumer and business confidence declines.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 exhibits positive returns in more than 50% of the 20-day periods after UNRATE surpasses 7%, the hypothesis is invalidated.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing real sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, which is likely to drive positive S&P 500 returns as corporate revenues and earnings grow.
failure_condition: If real sales growth is accompanied by negative S&P 500 returns in more than 30% of the 60-day windows, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL) may lead to tighter monetary policy, increasing borrowing costs and reducing corporate profitability, which could result in negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL remains above 240 but the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 60% of the 20-day periods, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising unemployment (UNRATE) and declining payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates labor market weakness, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns as economic growth falters.
failure_condition: If both UNRATE increases and PAYEMS decreases but the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 20-day windows, the hypothesis is invalidated.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing industrial production (INDPRO) suggests a strong supply chain and economic activity, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns as production and earnings increase.
failure_condition: If industrial production growth is accompanied by negative S&P 500 returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in real GDP (GDPC1) indicates reduced economic activity, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns as corporate revenues and earnings decline.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth slows but the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 60-day periods, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: While housing starts (HOUST) may indicate construction activity, a decline in real sales (RSAFS) suggests weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as economic growth slows.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases while RSAFS decreases but the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows, the hypothesis is invalidated.
